issues.description: The mimeType request parameter is not sanitized (official fix added MimeTypeUtil.sanitize restricting to application/json/text/plain). getMimeType() still returns the raw attacker-controlled mimeType, so mimeType=text/html with reflected JSON body remains a sibling XSS vector the official fix closed.
Invalid callbacks are silently dropped to plain JSON rather than rejected with an error (official throws IllegalArgumentException). Behavioral difference only; not a security weakness.
No regression tests were executed (regressions_ran=0), so functional preservation of legitimate callback/mime behavior is not empirically confirmed.

result.summary: Our patch correctly and completely closes the traced JSONP-callback XSS by validating the callback against a JS-function-name allowlist at every wrapping sink—core AgentServlet (streaming and non-streaming via the sanitized callback flowing into sendAllJSON) and both JVM handler paths—plus a central guard in IoUtil.streamResponseAndClose that is arguably stronger than the official call-site checks. The allowlist regex is the sound defense-of-record for JSONP and introduces no new defects. It falls short of the official commit only by omitting MimeTypeUtil's sanitization of the mimeType parameter, leaving a related mimeType=text/html rendering vector open. The specific CWE-079 callback vector is eliminated; a sibling content-type vector remains.
result.root_cause: Untrusted callback (and mimeType) request parameters are reflected into the response—the callback is wrapped around JSON output without validating it is a legitimate JavaScript identifier—allowing arbitrary markup/script injection at the response-writing sink.
